title: Exceptional external product is compatible with immersion direct images
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$. Work on their small pro-etale sites with bounded constructible constant-$A$ module complexes of finite Tor amplitude, denoted $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the geometric operations and specified constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility], and the external tensor product and canonical comparisons of [def-sf-kv-maps] specialized to $A$.

Let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ ($i=1,2$) be separated finite-type $k$-morphisms. Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow Y_1$ be either an open or a closed immersion, put $X_1'=X_1\times_{Y_1}Z$, and write $g':X_1'\to X_1$, $f_1':X_1'\to Z$. Put $f=f_1\times f_2$, $F=f_1'\times f_2$, $G=g\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2}$ and $G'=g'\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2}$. For the first-factor square let
$$D_{f_1,g}:f_1^!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*f_1'^!$$
be the inverse of the specified conjugate exchange of [def-trf-admissibility]; let $D_{f,G}:f^!RG_*\xrightarrow{\sim}RG'_*F^!$ denote the same comparison for the product square. Both are conjugates under the ordinary pullback/direct-image and constructible compact-support/exceptional adjunctions, as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_2,A)$ define $\sigma$ as
$$f_1^!Rg_*M\boxtimes f_2^!L\xrightarrow{D_{f_1,g}\boxtimes1}Rg'_*f_1'^!M\boxtimes f_2^!L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ku}_*}RG'_*(f_1'^!M\boxtimes f_2^!L),$$
and define $\tau$ as
$$f^!(Rg_*M\boxtimes L)\xrightarrow{f^!(\mathrm{Ku}_*)}f^!RG_*(M\boxtimes L)\xrightarrow{D_{f,G}}RG'_*F^!(M\boxtimes L),$$
where each $\mathrm{Ku}_*$ is the specified ordinary identity-factor comparison of [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth]. Then the equality of canonical morphisms
$$\tau\circ\alpha_{f_1,f_2}(Rg_*M,L)=RG'_*\bigl(\alpha_{f_1',f_2}(M,L)\bigr)\circ\sigma$$
holds, naturally in $M,L$. The analogous equality in the second variable holds after the signed tensor symmetry interchanges the two factors. All ordinary direct images here mean $R(-)_*$, including for an open immersion.

source.place: Paragraph 5: closed pushforward compatibility with alpha as an exceptional adjoint (mate-calculus check); paragraph 6: the same compatibility for open direct images; retained Step 10; the precise compatibility assertion is extracted from the retained stage-1 argument, rather than quoted as a separate theorem of the source.

proof.text: Use the adjunctions and their specified units and counits from [def-trf-admissibility]. Write $e_u:Lu^*Ru_*\to1$ for an ordinary counit and $\varepsilon_u:Ru_!u^!\to1$ for an exceptional counit. Abbreviate $P=f_1^!Rg_*M$, $Q=f_2^!L$, $K=P\boxtimes Q$, and $N=M\boxtimes L$. All these objects and the functors occurring in the statement are on the specified finite-Tor constructible domains: these are the restrictions stipulated in [def-trf-admissibility] and [def-sf-kv-maps]. Suppress $L$ on pullbacks and retain $R$ on direct images. Let $E_1:g^*Rf_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{1!}g'^*$ and $E:G^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}RF_!G'^*$ be the specified compact-support exchanges. The inverses of their conjugates are exactly the two maps $D$ in the question, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. No inverse of a general square mate is being asserted. The base-changed morphisms are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. For the witnessed domain of [fix-lem-exchanges] used below, choose étale-origin presentations of the bounded constructible objects by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). It applies at exactly this finite coefficient ring; no comparison of different coefficient categories is implicit.

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: the specified dual exchanges and adjunctions

proof.text:
Put $k_f=\mathrm{Ku}_{!,f_1,f_2}$ and $k_F=\mathrm{Ku}_{!,f'_1,f_2}$ as constructed in [def-sf-kv-maps](i). Their base-change identity at $(P,Q)$ is
$$k_F\circ E_K=(E_{1,P}\boxtimes1)\circ G^*(k_f).\tag{1}$$
Both sides start at $G^*Rf_!K$ and end at $Rf'_{1!}g'^*P\boxtimes Rf_{2!}Q$. Here and below pullback–tensor and pullback-composition identifications are the specified ones of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. To obtain (1), use the construction of $k_f$ over $T=Y_1\times Y_2$ in [def-sf-kv-maps](i): its relative product is for $X_1\times Y_2\to T$ and $Y_1\times X_2\to T$. Base-change this diagram by $G:Z\times Y_2\to T$. Clause (iii) of [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] identifies the pulled-back relative product with the relative product of these base changes. Its two remaining projection exchanges are the pulled-back projection exchanges in the definition of $k_f$. Pasting them with the first-factor square gives $E_1$, while the second factor is unchanged; the equality of these pasted exchanges is clause (2) of [fix-lem-exchanges]. This gives precisely (1), with no exceptional product comparison used.

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: the compact-support base-change square underlying the mate check

proof.text:
We need the ordinary comparisons with their counit normalization. For a morphism $u:V\to W$, put $H=u\times\operatorname{id}_S$ and denote its identity-factor comparison by $c_u:Ru_*B\boxtimes C\to RH_*(B\boxtimes C)$. Then
$$e_H\circ H^*c_u=e_u\boxtimes1.\tag{2}$$
The right side has source $u^*Ru_*B\boxtimes C$. Indeed the canonical comparison is projection base change $a^*Ru_*B\to RH_*b^*B$, tensored with the auxiliary pullback of $C$, followed by the ordinary projection map for $H$. In [def-exchange-projection] the first arrow is the mate of $b^*e_u$ and the second is the mate of the ordinary counit tensored with $1$. Applying the adjunct–counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] to these two formulas and naturality of the counit cancels the intervening unit: the result is $b^*e_u\otimes1$, which is (2). Monoidality of pullback is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Apply this calculation to $u=g,g'$. These are exactly the canonical comparisons specified by [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth], whose hypotheses hold for the finite coefficient ring and the separated finite-type schemes here. The calculation does not replace $Rj_*$ by $j_!$ when $u$ is open.

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: ordinary identity-factor comparisons; Stacks 07A7 and 0B56 counit formulas

proof.text:
Set
$$\theta=e_{g'}\circ g'^*(D_{f_1,g,M}):g'^*P\longrightarrow f_1'^!M,$$
and
$$t=e_g\circ g^*\varepsilon_{f_1,Rg_*M}\circ E_{1,P}^{-1}:Rf'_{1!}g'^*P\longrightarrow M.$$
These are exceptional adjoints:
$$\varepsilon_{f'_1,M}\circ Rf'_{1!}(\theta)=t.\tag{3}$$
Here is the direction check. The definition of the conjugate in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] identifies the Hom map induced by $D_{f_1,g}$ with
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,f_1^!Rg_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(g^*Rf_{1!}P,M)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(Rf'_{1!}g'^*P,M),$$
where the last map is precomposition by $E_{1,P}^{-1}$. The identity of $P$ becomes first $\varepsilon_{f_1,Rg_*M}$, then $e_g\circ g^*\varepsilon_{f_1,Rg_*M}$, and then $t$. On the other hand transposing $D_{f_1,g}$ first through $g'^*\dashv Rg'_*$ gives $\theta$. The pasted-adjunction rule [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) says that this iterated transpose is the same composite Hom map. The adjunct–counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] therefore gives (3).

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: inverse conjugate exchange evaluated at the identity

proof.text:
Compare the two proposed maps with the same bijection
$$\Psi:\operatorname{Hom}(K,RG'_*F^!N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(RF_!G'^*K,N),$$
$$\Psi(v)=\varepsilon_{F,N}\circ RF_!(e_{G'}\circ G'^*v).$$
The pasted-adjunction and change-of-adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3), applied to the conjugate of $E$, give
$$\Psi(D_{f,G}\circ f^!c_g\circ\alpha_f)
=e_G\circ G^*c_g\circ G^*(\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_!\alpha_f)\circ E_K^{-1}.$$
This is also obtained by the Hom calculation of Step 4, with $P$ replaced by $K$ and the identity replaced by $f^!c_g\circ\alpha_f$; naturality of the Hom bijections gives the displayed formula. By the definition of $\alpha_f$ in [def-sf-kv-maps](ii), its middle counit composite is $(\varepsilon_{f_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2})\circ k_f$. Substitute (2), then (1), and finally the definition of $t$. The result is
$$\Psi(\tau\circ\alpha_f)=(t\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,L})\circ k_F.\tag{4}$$
The source of $k_F$ in this formula is $RF_!(g'^*P\boxtimes Q)=RF_!G'^*K$.

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: explicit composite transpose of the upper path

proof.text:
For the other path, use the naturality of $e_{G'}$ and (2) for $g'$ to transpose its ordinary direct-image comparison. Its $G'^*\dashv RG'_*$ transpose is
$$\alpha_{f'_1,f_2}(M,L)\circ(\theta\boxtimes1_Q).$$
Transposing once more under $RF_!\dashv F^!$, the definition [def-sf-kv-maps](ii) of this $\alpha$ gives
$$(\varepsilon_{f'_1,M}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,L})\circ k_F\circ RF_!(\theta\boxtimes1).$$
Naturality of $k_F$ moves $\theta$ across $k_F$, so this equals
$$\bigl((\varepsilon_{f'_1,M}\circ Rf'_{1!}\theta)\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,L}\bigr)\circ k_F
=(t\boxtimes\varepsilon_{f_2,L})\circ k_F$$
by (3). This is exactly $\Psi(RG'_*(\alpha_{f'_1,f_2})\circ\sigma)$, and is the same arrow as (4).

source.place: paragraphs 5–6: explicit composite transpose of the lower path

proof.text: Injectivity of the adjunction bijection $\Psi$ proves the required equality. All constructions and bijections used above are natural in $M,L$, so the equality is natural. For the second-variable assertion interchange the two pairs $(X_i,Y_i,f_i)$. The signed tensor symmetry identifies the two external products by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Clause (i) of [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence], applied to the relative product in the construction [def-sf-kv-maps](i), identifies the swapped compact-support Künneth map with the original one through those symmetries. Taking its exceptional transpose, with the counits interchanged, identifies the swapped $\alpha$ with the conjugate of the original $\alpha$ by these same symmetries. For the ordinary comparison the identical assertion follows directly by swapping the counit and identity in (2). Thus the proved first-variable equality for the relabelled diagram is the asserted second-variable equality, with exactly the signed symmetries specified in the question.
